items.s: There is no magic ____ for a bad mood, but a walk can help.

items.s: Researchers ____ how time in nature affects our minds for many years.
A review ____ in 2025 examined experiments with adults.
People may feel calmer after ____ time outside.
Last week, a friend ____ me to a small park near her house.
You do not need ____ every step.

tfn.s: The evidence for memory and concentration was equally strong.
tfn.why: The text says the opposite: "The evidence that nature improves memory and concentration was much weaker."

tfn.s: Not everybody can reach good green spaces easily.
tfn.why: The text says: "Of course, access to nature is not equal."

tfn.s: The review suggested that time in nature can lift people's mood.
tfn.why: The text says: "It found good evidence that natural places can improve people's mood."

tfn.s: The review was paid for by a government.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text does not say who paid for the review.

tfn.s: The writer says people must count every step for a walk to help.
tfn.why: The text says: "You do not need to count every step."

focus.note: Collocations are words that go together naturally. Learn the pair, not just the single word.

tfn.s: All the studies in the review measured stress in the same way.
tfn.why: The text says results for stress "depended partly on how stress was measured".

tfn.s: The writer thinks cities should stop creating green spaces because the benefits are unclear.
tfn.why: The text says the complexity "should not put cities off creating accessible green spaces".

tfn.s: Someone near a safe park has more chances to go outside regularly than a person in a neighbourhood with no safe park.
tfn.why: The text compares someone near "a safe, attractive park" with a person in a neighbourhood with poor facilities.

tfn.s: The researchers who wrote the review work at a university.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text does not say where the researchers work.

tfn.s: Walking with a friend makes it easy to say which part of the walk helps most.
tfn.why: The text says a walk with a friend makes it "difficult to isolate one factor".

focus.note: Fixed pairs are often a verb plus noun or an adjective plus noun. Ask which word people usually choose, not only which word fits the meaning.

items.s: The effects of the treatment proved far less ____ than the doctors had hoped.

tfn.s: Both 2025 reviews gave strong support to the idea that nature improves attention.
tfn.why: The first review found attention findings inconsistent, and the second suggested only "modest" benefits.

tfn.s: The writer argues that the research should mainly be used to urge individuals to spend more time outdoors.
tfn.why: The writer says policymakers should treat it as evidence for accessible public spaces, "rather than" another instruction to individuals.

tfn.s: Advice to visit nature would be harder to follow in a neighbourhood with heavy traffic and few public transport links.
tfn.why: Residents of such areas "may come up against obstacles that personal motivation cannot solve".

tfn.s: The reviews included studies carried out in more than one country.
tfn.why: Not stated. The text does not say where the studies took place.

tfn.s: The two reviews appeared in the same month.
tfn.why: Only the first review's month (November 2025) is given; the second is just "a second 2025 review".

focus.note: Test each pair for register as well as meaning. Fluent writers expect a particular adjective, verb or noun in formal phrases.

speak.title: Role-play: our local park
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.text: You have money for one job in the park this year: new lights, new benches or a new path. Ask the resident two questions, then decide what to offer. You can say yes, no, or yes to part of the request.

b.text: The park near your home is hard to enjoy. The path is broken and there are no benches. Ask the council to fix it, explain who needs it most, and try to get a date.

phrases: I'd like to talk about the park near my house.
It's hard for older people to use it.
We've only got money for one thing this year.
I'm afraid I can't promise a date.
Could we agree on a small first step?
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class what the council decided and whether you think it was fair.
